policy_title: New Accessibility Standards for Public Spaces and UN CRPD Incorporation
stated: Make it easier for disabled people to access public life, including the world of work, by: Adopting new accessibility standards for public spaces. Improving the legislative framework for blue badges. Incorporating the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities into UK law.

source.quote: Make it easier for disabled people to access public life, including the world of work, by: Adopting new accessibility standards for public spaces. Improving the legislative framework for blue badges. Incorporating the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities into UK law.

bearing_set.reason: Incorporating the UN CRPD into UK law directly creates an enforceable legal rights and equal-treatment framework for disabled people, squarely within O9's scope of anti-discrimination protections and due process.

The policy explicitly targets access to 'the world of work' for disabled people; accessibility standards in public spaces and blue badge improvements directly reduce structural barriers to employment and job participation for disabled people, a non-negligible effect on employment rates and job access for this group.

membership_note: The two non-negligible bearings are equal treatment (O9, the primary legal mechanism) and labour-market access for disabled people (O4, explicitly in scope). Aggregate prosperity (O13) and personal liberty (O10) effects are either too indirect or too small to clear the non-negligible bar.
